q: Does the paper's method-ranking-by-shot-budget claim (VD/ZNE win at N_tot=1e5-1e7, CDR/vnCDR at 1e7-1e9, UNITED at 1e10) survive when the underlying noise model is swapped from IonQ trapped-ion to a superconducting-transmon noise model (IBM Falcon/Eagle-style, with correlated ZZ crosstalk, T1/T2 asymmetry, and measurement error)?
basis: Paper's benchmark is single-noise-model (trapped-ion, Appendix H). Our replication used Qiskit Aer local depolarizing (different regime again). QEM method rankings are famously noise-structure-sensitive (e.g. PEC failing in our stack is a representation-mismatch, not a shot problem). The paper's headline could over-generalize from one hardware family.
next_steps: Reproduce the paper's ZNE/CDR/vnCDR pipeline (Mitiq for ZNE/CDR/vnCDR; UNITED implemented as CDR-on-VD-corrected data as described in the paper's Sec 4) on (a) Qiskit Aer FakeSherbrooke/FakeCairoV2 noise models (free, calibrated to real IBM hardware), and (b) the paper's original trapped-ion model as a sanity anchor. Run at Q in {4,6,8}, N_tot in {1e6,1e8,1e10}. Diff the winning-method-by-budget table. All on free Qiskit Aer, no cloud.

q: Does modern QEM beyond the paper's set --- specifically Subspace Expansion (SE), Symmetry Verification (SV), and Learning-Based PEC / probabilistic error cancellation with GST-learned representations --- change the Pareto frontier of accuracy vs. sampling cost that the paper reports for the four data-driven methods (ZNE, CDR, vnCDR, VD, UNITED)?
basis: Paper (2021, updated 2023) predates or omits several QEM techniques that have since matured: subspace expansion (McClean 2020), Mitiq's learning-based PEC (Strikis 2020, Mitiq >=0.28), and generalized virtual distillation variants (ESD). If any of these dominate a corner of the paper's cost/accuracy plot, the 'UNITED wins at 1e10' story is a moving target.
next_steps: Extend the paper's benchmark harness: add Mitiq's PEC-with-learning-based-representations and Mitiq's subspace_expansion module as additional QEM contenders on the same random-quantum-circuit and QAOA-Max-Cut suites, at Q in {4,6,8}. Score them on the paper's own accuracy metric (|est - exact|) and their sample-complexity cost (total shots consumed, including any calibration/training shots). Regenerate the paper's Fig 3/4 style shot-budget curves with the enlarged method set. Report which new methods dominate which N_tot regimes.

q: Is there a *problem-adaptive* method-selection rule --- e.g. a classical decision tree taking (Q, depth, circuit-family fingerprint like operator-norm distance from Clifford, and target N_tot) as input and outputting the predicted best-of-{ZNE, CDR, vnCDR, VD, UNITED} for that circuit --- that would systematically beat 'always pick UNITED', which is the paper's implicit large-budget recommendation?
basis: The paper shows the winning method depends on shot budget AND on the circuit (QAOA vs RQC give different curves). But the paper does not propose or evaluate an *adaptive selector*. Practitioners currently must either guess or run all four; if an ~O(circuit) classical predictor exists, it changes the deployment story from 'run UNITED' to 'run the predicted-best'.
next_steps: Build a training set: for each (Q, depth, circuit-family, N_tot) tuple in the paper's benchmark, compute the empirical winner among {ZNE, CDR, vnCDR, VD, UNITED-approx}. Train a small classifier (random forest / gradient boosting) on cheap circuit features (2-design distance, Clifford fraction, entanglement entropy of the ideal state, mean 2-qubit gate density). Evaluate hold-out predictive accuracy of winner selection, and average |err| gain of adaptive selection vs. always-UNITED, on a fresh held-out benchmark suite. Free compute: Qiskit Aer + scikit-learn.

q: How does the paper's UNITED estimator interact with *algorithmic* error mitigation (e.g. echo verification / SWAP-test-based purity extrapolation, mid-circuit measurement-based post-selection, error-detected encoded computation on repetition or [[4,2,2]] codes) --- specifically, is there a composition rule where 'algorithmic EM inside, UNITED outside' gives an additive-in-decibels error reduction, or does it saturate / interfere?
basis: UNITED is presented as a monolithic post-processing composite. The next 2 years of QEM literature has emphasized *stacking* mitigations (algorithmic-inside-hardware, hardware-inside-post-processing). The paper does not address composability with the algorithmic layer, but that is where the field is headed for early-fault-tolerant quantum computing.
next_steps: Design a stacked benchmark: pick a small algorithmic EM (e.g. post-selection on a [[4,2,2]] Bacon-Shor patch, or echo verification via forward-inverse circuit pairing) applicable to a subset of the paper's benchmark circuits. Run three configurations: (i) algorithmic EM alone, (ii) UNITED alone, (iii) algorithmic-then-UNITED stacked. Measure |err| reduction in each and check whether stacked >= max(algo, UNITED) and whether the improvement is multiplicative in error-suppression factor. Free stack: Qiskit + Mitiq + Stim (for code simulation).

q: Does the paper's ranking of QEM methods hold on *current* NISQ hardware runtimes (IBM Heron r2/Fez, IonQ Forte-1, Rigetti Ankaa-3), where real device drift, non-Markovian noise, and calibration-cycle timing dominate --- and specifically, is CDR still a viable direct-paper method when the classical near-Clifford training oracle has to model calibration drift within a single execution window?
basis: The paper is a simulator-based benchmark. Real 2026-era NISQ devices have (a) intra-experiment calibration drift, (b) non-Markovian correlated errors (spectator crosstalk, TLS defects), and (c) reset/measurement overheads that dominate PEC/vnCDR sample budgets. The paper's shot-budget accounting silently assumes stationary Markovian noise per shot; this is optimistic on hardware.
next_steps: Use free IBM Quantum Network access (Open Plan, up to 10 min/mo on Heron r2/Fez) to run a scaled-down version of the paper's Q=4, depth<=16 subset with ZNE and CDR under Mitiq. Do NOT use pay-per-shot IonQ/Rigetti (not free). For each hardware run, also log the ibm_calibrations JSON at run-start and run-end and quantify calibration drift. Compare hardware ZNE/CDR |err| improvement factor against the paper's simulator prediction; report whether the improvement multiplier degrades by (approximately) 2x on hardware and whether CDR's classical oracle assumption breaks under observed drift.
